nodes.name: Tank 01
nodes.speaker: Narrator
nodes.dialogue: A punch bowl and a broken elevator meet below an upstairs party.{pause}Guntank carries the bowl on a tray fitted neatly across his treads.{pause}Guncannon carries cups, candles, and a cake with serious frosting.{pause}The elevator button glows, clicks, and displays OUT FOR THINKING.{pause}Music thumps from the second floor like a cheerful distant heartbeat.{pause}The first guest arrives in twenty-five minutes with no idea where to go.{pause}A gift balloon waits beside the bowl, confident that stairs are somebody else's problem.

nodes.name: Tank 02
nodes.speaker: Guntank
nodes.dialogue: Stairs acknowledged. I have calculated several optimistic angles.{pause}The staircase rises in two flights with one narrow turning landing.{pause}Each step is taller than his front tread prefers to discuss.{pause}The punch surface trembles whenever he rotates toward the first riser.{pause}Guncannon removes the tray and places it safely on the lobby table.{pause}They agree the robot climbs before the fruit beverage attempts anything.{pause}Guntank marks the bowl SAFE and himself PENDING in the plan.

nodes.name: Tank 03
nodes.speaker: Guncannon
nodes.dialogue: Two folding tables make a ramp. Three make a legacy.{pause}The lobby contains six tables intended for cake, gifts, and card games.{pause}Their legs lock firmly, though one table lists slightly to the left.{pause}Guntank checks the hinges, weight limits, and decorative tablecloths.{pause}One label says NOT FOR VEHICLES in handwriting added this morning.{pause}Guncannon turns the label over and calls it unhelpful timing.{pause}The tablecloth hides the warning but does not improve engineering.

nodes.name: Tank 04
nodes.speaker: Host
nodes.dialogue: The party room is upstairs because it has windows and a sound system.{pause}The lobby has outlets, wide doors, and no view beyond the coat rack.{pause}The host offers to carry Guntank, then tries lifting one tread.{pause}Guntank politely thanks him before the attempt becomes a back injury.{pause}Guncannon asks which parts of the party truly require the second floor.{pause}The host says cake, friends, and birthday dignity, in that order.{pause}He admits dignity has no reservation form and might relocate.

nodes.name: Tank 05
nodes.speaker: SYSTEM
nodes.dialogue: Available equipment: six tables, twelve chairs, one hand truck.{pause}Also present: rope, nonslip mats, balloons, and a welcome banner.{pause}The hand truck squeaks under an empty cup and withdraws from consideration.{pause}Balloons add morale but no measurable lifting capacity.{pause}Guntank assigns each item a role in three possible plans.{pause}Guncannon quietly removes balloons from the structural category.

nodes.name: Tank 06
nodes.speaker: Narrator
nodes.dialogue: They test one stair with no cargo and three people watching.{pause}Guntank raises his front tread, meets the edge, and advances one inch.{pause}His back tread remains in the lobby with strong personal opinions.{pause}Guncannon braces from the side while the host guards the wall paint.{pause}After ten seconds, Guntank returns to level ground by mutual agreement.{pause}The audience applauds the test because it ended without paperwork.

nodes.name: Tank 07
nodes.speaker: Guntank
nodes.dialogue: My wheels are not a mistake. They are excellent on almost every floor.{pause}Guncannon says a staircase is a floor that forgot to stay together.{pause}The joke helps, but Guntank keeps looking toward the party music.{pause}He wants to arrive as a guest, not as a problem everyone carries.{pause}The host says changing the room would not change who the party honors.{pause}Guntank stores that thought beside his most realistic calculations.{pause}Guntank remembers a museum trip where everyone took the front stairs before noticing the side{pause}entrance had become a storage corridor.{pause}He waited beside stacked boxes until a guard moved them, then arrived after the guide had finished{pause}describing his favorite exhibit.{pause}The apology was sincere, but the lost explanation could not be replayed, and Guntank had pretended{pause}it did not matter.{pause}Today he tells the host plainly: joining late is not the same as being welcomed from the{pause}beginning.

nodes.name: Tank 08
nodes.speaker: Narrator
nodes.dialogue: They pause while sunlight stretches across the quiet lobby tiles.{pause}The title melody returns beneath the muffled music from upstairs.{pause}Guncannon lights no candles yet, but counts every one twice.{pause}Guntank watches his reflection in the elevator's closed metal door.{pause}The OUT FOR THINKING sign changes to STILL THINKING.{pause}For one minute, nobody asks machinery to prove anything.

nodes.name: Tank 09
nodes.speaker: Host
nodes.dialogue: First guests report five minutes away. We need an initial climb plan.{pause}A folding-table ramp could bridge each set of three steps.{pause}A stair relay could move cargo upward while Guntank tests each riser alone.{pause}The ramp risks hinges but offers a continuous tread surface.{pause}The relay protects supplies but leaves Guntank facing every step.{pause}Both plans need spotters, patience, and the absence of punch.

nodes.name: Tank 10
nodes.speaker: Guncannon
nodes.dialogue: We can build the ramp slowly, checking every locked leg.{pause}Or we can stage a step-by-step ascent with mats and resting points.{pause}One plan uses furniture as engineering with very polite permission.{pause}The other uses the stairs as designed, which is rude but honest.{pause}Guntank wants the choice that keeps helpers safe and dignity intact.{pause}He selects how the team will attempt the first flight.

nodes.name: Tank A1
nodes.speaker: Guncannon
nodes.dialogue: Table ramp plan. Two tables make a ramp, three make a legacy.{pause}They lock the first table flat from lobby floor to the third step.{pause}A nonslip mat protects its surface and the table's remaining pride.{pause}The second table bridges toward the landing with chairs as side rails.{pause}Guntank inspects every hinge while the host signs off on cake-table duty.{pause}The improvised road looks brave, level, and deeply against its instincts.

nodes.name: Tank A2
nodes.speaker: Narrator
nodes.dialogue: Guntank climbs six centimeters with historic resolve.{pause}His treads grip the mat while three spotters hold the side rails.{pause}The table gives one small creak, and everyone freezes respectfully.{pause}Guncannon checks the lock, adds rope, and approves another inch.{pause}Progress becomes a sequence of tiny movements and enormous announcements.{pause}The first guest arrives just in time to cheer centimeter nine.

nodes.name: Tank A3
nodes.speaker: Guest
nodes.dialogue: Is this the entertainment or should I take off my shoes?{pause}The host says both, then assigns the guest to guard the cake.{pause}More arrivals hold chairs, carry cups, and keep the lobby path clear.{pause}Guntank moves from being a problem to leading a community project.{pause}At halfway, he pauses and asks every helper to check their hands.{pause}Nobody is strained, the ramp is stable, and the cake remains distant.

nodes.name: Tank A4
nodes.speaker: Guntank
nodes.dialogue: First flight complete. Tables one and two may retire with honor.{pause}He reaches the landing and rotates without touching either wall.{pause}Guests carry the ramp pieces up for a possible second deployment.{pause}Guncannon brings the cups but leaves punch and cake below.{pause}The climb took twelve minutes and gathered an audience of nine.{pause}They meet the turning landing with equipment, confidence, and no beverages.

nodes.name: Tank B1
nodes.speaker: Guntank
nodes.dialogue: Mats and relay stations. We will respect every individual stair.{pause}Nonslip pads cover the first three edges while chairs mark rest points.{pause}Guests carry cups and decorations upward in a two-way line.{pause}Guncannon stays beside Guntank, calling tread angles before each move.{pause}The host waits one step above with rope held loose, never pulling.{pause}The ascent begins like a very slow dance taught by civil engineers.

nodes.name: Tank B2
nodes.speaker: Narrator
nodes.dialogue: Front tread rises. Back tread follows. Both settle on one mat.{pause}Guntank pauses at each step while the supply relay passes beside him.{pause}Balloons float upward, followed by cups, plates, and wrapped gifts.{pause}The cake remains below because nobody trusts frosting on stairs.{pause}At step four, Guntank learns to turn slightly before lifting.{pause}The movement looks less heroic than a ramp and feels more his own.

nodes.name: Tank B3
nodes.speaker: Guncannon
nodes.dialogue: Angle good. Left tread good. Please ignore the balloon on your cannon.{pause}A red balloon has tied itself to Guntank's shoulder mount.{pause}It bobs with every step, making the serious operation look festive.{pause}Guntank keeps it because guests use the balloon to track progress.{pause}The relay chants STEP, SETTLE, PASS whenever he reaches a new mat.{pause}Their rhythm carries him to the final stair of the first flight.

nodes.name: Tank B4
nodes.speaker: Guntank
nodes.dialogue: Landing reached under my own power, with nine mats and one balloon.{pause}He thanks every spotter before rotating toward the second flight.{pause}Guests have already moved decorations, music sheets, and half the chairs.{pause}Guncannon leaves cake and punch below under careful guard.{pause}The stair plan was slower, but every movement can be repeated safely.{pause}They meet the turning landing with a practiced relay and dry supplies.

nodes.name: Tank 11
nodes.speaker: Narrator
nodes.dialogue: The main tune returns as everyone studies the second flight.{pause}It is steeper, narrower, and missing a handrail near the top.{pause}The remaining tables cannot open fully on the small landing.{pause}Mats can cover the steps, but spotters have nowhere safe to stand.{pause}Guntank could continue only with much greater risk and less help.{pause}Below, the lobby has quietly filled with arriving guests.

nodes.name: Tank 12
nodes.speaker: Host
nodes.dialogue: We proved the first flight is possible. We do not have to prove both.{pause}The host checks upstairs: windows, sound system, empty tables.{pause}Then he checks downstairs: friends, punch, cake, and one tired Guntank.{pause}Guncannon says a party is already forming around the equipment pile.{pause}Someone plugs a small speaker into the lobby outlet.{pause}The coat rack receives a balloon crown and becomes decoration.

nodes.name: Tank 13
nodes.speaker: Guntank
nodes.dialogue: If we stop now, I climbed one flight to return where I began.{pause}Guncannon says returning with information is not returning unchanged.{pause}The first flight taught them which equipment works and where risk grows.{pause}Guests learned how to carry supplies without blocking the stairs.{pause}The host learned the lobby holds more people than the upstairs room.{pause}Guntank learned asking for help can still leave the decision his.{pause}The host gathers the guests who worked the first flight and asks what they actually enjoyed{pause}about the climb.{pause}They name the careful rhythm, the balloon navigator, and the moment Guntank stopped the{pause}operation to check every spotter's hands.{pause}Nobody names the upstairs room; several guests have not even seen it, and one thought the lobby was{pause}always the reception space.{pause}Guntank realizes the valuable part of the attempt may already be present in the people who{pause}learned to move together.

nodes.name: Tank 14
nodes.speaker: Guest
nodes.dialogue: Why not split the party? Music upstairs and food downstairs.{pause}Another guest points out that half a birthday is not easy to sing to.{pause}The host wants everybody together for candles and the first toast.{pause}Guntank offers to become a lobby table for cake and gifts.{pause}Guncannon says his shoulder is exactly punch-bowl height.{pause}The practical joke begins sounding like a practical floor plan.

nodes.name: Tank 15
nodes.speaker: SYSTEM
nodes.dialogue: Option one: rebuild a shorter ramp and attempt the second flight.{pause}Punch and cake would travel separately after Guntank reaches the top.{pause}Option two: move remaining chairs down and open the lobby party.{pause}The upstairs room would become a quiet coat and gift lounge.{pause}Both options preserve the celebration, but only one preserves the address.{pause}The elevator updates its sign to THANK YOU FOR YOUR PATIENCE.

nodes.name: Tank 16
nodes.speaker: Guntank
nodes.dialogue: I wanted the stairs to stop being something I could not do.{pause}The title melody returns while the red balloon taps his cannon.{pause}Guncannon says doing one hard flight already changed that sentence.{pause}The host says the birthday never required a second-floor victory.{pause}Guntank looks up at the narrow rise, then down at the waiting crowd.{pause}He can choose challenge, welcome, or the place where both meet.{pause}Guntank asks whether choosing the lobby would make the careful first flight pointless, and the{pause}room answers with an immediate chorus of no.{pause}The mats now have measured spacing, the guests know safe relay positions, and the host has already{pause}added access questions to future invitations.{pause}Finishing could still be joyful, but stopping would also leave behind knowledge instead of{pause}shame.{pause}The choice becomes less about defeating stairs and more about deciding which lesson the birthday{pause}should carry upstairs.

nodes.name: Tank 17
nodes.speaker: Narrator
nodes.dialogue: The cake candles wait unlit and the punch bowl waits safely below.{pause}Guests hold ramp ropes, folding chairs, gifts, and paper cups.{pause}Nobody complains about the delay; they are watching Guntank decide.{pause}Continuing would turn the ascent into the party's great adventure.{pause}Returning would turn the lobby into a room designed around everyone.{pause}The main tune resumes as Guntank calls for the final vote.

nodes.name: Tank C1
nodes.speaker: Guntank
nodes.dialogue: We finish carefully. Short ramp, extra rope, no audience on the stairs.{pause}Guests clear both flights while Guncannon rebuilds one table section.{pause}The host checks every lock and places mats above and below.{pause}Guntank climbs from the landing in movements smaller than before.{pause}Nobody chants now; spotters speak only the next useful instruction.{pause}At the top, his front tread touches level floor and stays there.

nodes.name: Tank C2
nodes.speaker: Narrator
nodes.dialogue: Guntank reaches the party room to a cheer heard from the lobby.{pause}He immediately radios that the route is safe for supplies, not robots.{pause}The punch begins its ascent in a bowl carried by six careful hands.{pause}Cake follows in its box while candles travel in one guest's pocket.{pause}The bowl reaches the upper landing first and waits like a champion.{pause}Guntank positions himself beside the window and finally sees the view.

nodes.name: Tank C3
nodes.speaker: Guncannon
nodes.dialogue: Two tables made a ramp. Three made a legacy. Six made furniture again.{pause}After the final trip, every table opens flat for food and games.{pause}One bears a chalk mark showing Guntank's historic centimeter nine.{pause}Guests toast the climb, then spend the evening talking about other things.{pause}The ascent tune softens as cake, punch, and friends share one room.{pause}The elevator sign changes to MAYBE TOMORROW and receives no attention.

nodes.name: Tank C4
nodes.speaker: Guntank
nodes.dialogue: I took the stairs, but the stairs were never mine alone.{pause}He thanks ramp builders, mat layers, spotters, and punch carriers.{pause}The host saves the red balloon and names it First Flight Navigator.{pause}Future invitations include an access check before any room is booked.{pause}Guntank keeps the nonslip mat that met his first successful tread.{pause}Next year, the party chooses ground level with excellent windows.

nodes.name: Tank D1
nodes.speaker: Guntank
nodes.dialogue: Lobby party. Bring every chair down. I will become the cake table.{pause}He descends the practiced first flight with mats and spotters in place.{pause}Guests form a relay around him, carrying decorations toward the lobby.{pause}The host moves the speaker, and Guncannon guards the punch bowl.{pause}By the time Guntank reaches tile, balloons fill the coat rack.{pause}Returning feels less like retreat and more like opening the front door.

nodes.name: Tank D2
nodes.speaker: Narrator
nodes.dialogue: The lobby becomes a party room in seven cooperative minutes.{pause}Folding tables hold food instead of attempting careers in transportation.{pause}Guntank parks beside the cake with gifts arranged across his tray.{pause}Children hang the red balloon from his cannon and add two blue ones.{pause}The upstairs room becomes a quiet place for coats and tired guests.{pause}The broken elevator is no longer the center of anybody's plan.

nodes.name: Tank D3
nodes.speaker: Guncannon
nodes.dialogue: The lobby requests a birthday encore every week.{pause}Wide doors welcome late guests, and windows are replaced by open doors.{pause}The coat rack remains crowned, the cake table remains mobile.{pause}Guntank leads a tread-and-tiptoe dance that stays perfectly level.{pause}The lobby tune fills the whole first floor and reaches the sidewalk.{pause}People passing outside join the final chorus without climbing anything.

nodes.name: Tank D4
nodes.speaker: Host
nodes.dialogue: Best party we nearly held somewhere else.{pause}The host adds ACCESSIBLE GROUND FLOOR to every future invitation.{pause}Guntank receives the first cake slice from his own tray-table.{pause}Guncannon toasts the six centimeters that changed the entire event.{pause}The elevator finally opens after cleanup and finds an empty lobby.{pause}Its display reads READY. Guntank presses CLOSE and rolls home laughing.
